tldr: OpenAI Gym is a toolkit for reinforcement learning research providing a common interface for diverse benchmark environments and a website for sharing and comparing algorithm results.
contributions: A software package combining best elements of previous RL benchmark collections (ALE, RLLab) with maximal convenience and accessibility
A growing collection of benchmark environments with a common interface, versioned for reproducibility
A website (gym.openai.com) with scoreboards for comparing algorithm performance
Design emphasizing sample complexity alongside final performance and encouraging peer review over competition
methods: The authors designed OpenAI Gym based on their experience developing and comparing reinforcement learning algorithms and using previous benchmark collections. The toolkit provides environment abstractions (not agent abstractions) supporting both online learning and batch update styles. Environments are formalized as partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) in an episodic setting. At initial beta release, the toolkit included classic control tasks, algorithmic tasks, Atari games via ALE, Go (9x9 and 19x19) via Pachi engine, and 2D/3D robots via MuJoCo physics engine.
results: The paper describes the toolkit's design rather than experimental results. The initial release included environments spanning classic control, algorithmic computation tasks (e.g., multi-digit addition, sequence reversal), Atari 2600 games, Go board games, and robot simulation tasks. Future work mentions potential additions including Box2D-based and Doom-based environments. A Monitor component was included by default, tracking every timestep and reset, capable of recording videos and producing learning curves.
limitations: The toolkit focuses on the episodic setting only. It does not include an agent class or specify agent interfaces, leaving that to users. The paper acknowledges that RL benchmarking is more challenging than supervised learning due to difficulties in measuring generalization without hidden test sets. The current tasks are meant to be solved from scratch, with no built-in support for curriculum or transfer learning.
